askExpert.intro: Have a question about your rights? A trained volunteer from a partner legal aid organisation answers privately.
askExpert.safetyNote: Don't write your full name, address, school or phone number.
askExpert.submittedMessage: Your question is sent. Only a verified volunteer can see it. Answers usually come within 2 days.

answered.q: Can a school refuse admission if I don't have a birth certificate?
answered.a: No. Under the RTE Act, no child can be denied admission because they don't have age proof. The school can use other documents or a declaration from your parents.

answered.q: My friend is 13 and works full-time at a shop. Is that legal?
answered.a: No. Children under 14 can't be employed in shops. You can tell a teacher, or an adult can call 1098 or report it on the PENCIL portal.

answered.q: My cousin is 16 and her family wants her to marry. What can we do?
answered.a: That would be a child marriage, which is a crime. Call 1098 or tell a teacher or Anganwadi worker. A Child Marriage Prohibition Officer can stop it.

answered.q: Someone online keeps asking for my photos. What should I do?
answered.a: Don't send anything, and block them. Tell a trusted adult. You can also report it to the Cyber Crime Helpline, 1930.

answered.q: Do I have to pay a lawyer if I need legal help?
answered.a: No. Children can get free legal help from the Legal Services Authority in their district. The national legal aid helpline is 15100.

answered.q: Is a teacher allowed to hit me if I don't do my homework?
answered.a: No. The RTE Act bans physical punishment and mental harassment in school. Tell your parents or the headteacher.
